title: Hari Lal v. District Magistrate, Azamgarh
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Naheed Ara Moonis, J. and Saumitra Dayal Singh, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; relegated to statutory Supply Code appeal.
headnote: A writ seeking to quash a recovery certificate dated 10 August 2020 and an order dated 4 February 2021, and to restrain coercive recovery, was dismissed because that order was a final order under Clause 6.8(d)(i) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, for which a statutory appeal lay. The High Court allowed two weeks to file the appeal and directed that it be decided expeditiously without objection if so filed.
facts: Hari Lal sought certiorari to quash a recovery certificate dated 10 August 2020 and an order dated 4 February 2021 of respondent no.3, and a mandamus against coercive recovery as arrears of land revenue or by arrest. On 23 June 2021 his counsel was not on the video link; the petition was listed as fresh for 15 July 2021 with instructions to be obtained. At the adjourned hearing the respondent-corporation treated the 4 February 2021 order as a Supply Code final order.

holding_units.holding: An order of the licensee under Clause 6.8(d)(i) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is a final order. A writ petition seeking to quash that order and the consequential recovery certificate, and to restrain coercive recovery as arrears of land revenue or by arrest, is not maintainable when a statutory appeal is available. The petition was dismissed on the ground of alternative remedy, with liberty to file the appeal within two weeks, to be decided expeditiously without objection.

principle_tags.application: The Court accepted that the 4 February 2021 order was a final order under Clause 6.8(d)(i) carrying a statutory appeal, dismissed the writ on that alternative remedy, and protected a two-week filing window.

not_decided.point: validity of the recovery certificate dated 10.08.2020 and the order dated 04.02.2021
not_decided.note: The Court did not examine the merits of either instrument, dismissing solely on alternative remedy.
